subject.title: fix: deleting a session leaves its trajectory artifacts orphaned on disk

question: Should reset and delete retain trajectory tool-call records under the same archive retention policy as transcripts, including when trajectories live in an operator-configured external directory?
rationale: The patch intentionally changes the privacy, forensic-retention, and external-directory cleanup boundary; tests can establish mechanics but cannot choose that product/security policy.

options.title: Approve coupled tombstones
options.body: Retain trajectory runtime and pointer artifacts with transcript-matching reset/delete suffixes and retention, after fixing durable retirement and preserving strict ownership checks.

options.title: Narrow to delete cleanup
options.body: Land only the original delete-orphan repair and leave reset preservation to the dedicated reset issue and PR.

options.title: Keep trajectories ephemeral
options.body: Reject reset-time trajectory retention and implement safe deletion without retaining sensitive trajectory archives.

recommendation.title: Approve coupled tombstones
recommendation.body: Retain trajectory runtime and pointer artifacts with transcript-matching reset/delete suffixes and retention, after fixing durable retirement and preserving strict ownership checks.

likelyOwner.reason: He is the assigned reviewer and strongest current-main history owner for the affected trajectory and session lifecycle paths.
